newsitem.title: USA: CBOT SOYOIL LOWER ON OVERBOUGHT IDEAS, MEAL MIXED.
newsitem.headline: CBOT SOYOIL LOWER ON OVERBOUGHT IDEAS, MEAL MIXED.

text.p: Ideas that CBOT soyoil futures were overbought prompted early selling on Wednesday, and soymeal sales were mixed, traders said.
"There is more talk of China (soy)oil business, but a lot of people think the market's overdone," said one floor trader.
On Tuesday, there was widespread talk among soyoil traders that China was seeking U.S. soyoil for September and October shipment. U.S. exporters couldn't confirm a sale, however.
U.S. soyoil prices are now said to be competitive with South American values, so exports could pick up soon, traders said.

Tuesday's USDA outlook for a record U.S. soybean crop this year and generally good crop weather this week in the U.S. Midwest should limit gains in new crop contracts for soymeal and soyoil, traders said.

At 1020 CDT, December soyoil was down 0.23 at 22.39 cent a lb and other months were down 0.23 to 0.29 cents. December soymeal was $0.30 per ton lower at $199.00 a ton, and other months were $2.10 higher to $0.50 lower.
